question: What Is An API Endpoint?
answerGeneral: An API endpoint is a specific URL where an API can be accessed and a particular operation performed. It's the point of entry for a request. Each endpoint combines a URL path and an HTTP method to represent a specific action on a resource. For example: GET /api/questions returns all questions, POST /api/questions creates a new question, GET /api/questions/42 returns question 42. The base URL (e.g. https://api.myapp.com) plus the path (e.g. /questions/42) forms the full endpoint URL. Endpoints form the 'surface area' of an API — designing them well makes the API intuitive and easy to use.
answerGeneralTr: Bir API endpoint'i, bir API'ye erişilebilen ve belirli bir işlemin gerçekleştirilebildiği özel bir URL'dir. Her endpoint, bir kaynak üzerindeki belirli bir eylemi temsil etmek için bir URL yolu ve HTTP metodunu birleştirir. Örneğin: GET /api/questions tüm soruları döndürür, POST /api/questions yeni bir soru oluşturur. Temel URL artı yol tam endpoint URL'sini oluşturur. Endpoint'ler bir API'nin 'yüzey alanını' oluşturur — onları iyi tasarlamak API'yi sezgisel ve kullanımı kolay hale getirir.

## API Endpoints

## Anatomy of an Endpoint

```
https://api.myapp.com/v1/questions/42
│─────────────────────│─────│───────│
  Base URL              Path   Resource ID

+  HTTP Method (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE)
= A specific operation on a specific resource
```

## Endpoint Examples

```
Collection endpoints (no ID):
  GET    /questions        → List all questions
  POST   /questions        → Create a new question

Resource endpoints (with ID):
  GET    /questions/42     → Get question 42
  PUT    /questions/42     → Replace question 42
  PATCH  /questions/42     → Partially update question 42
  DELETE /questions/42     → Delete question 42

Nested resource endpoints:
  GET    /questions/42/comments   → Comments on question 42
  POST   /questions/42/comments   → Add comment to question 42

Action endpoints:
  POST   /questions/42/bookmark   → Bookmark question 42
  DELETE /questions/42/bookmark   → Remove bookmark
```

## Endpoint vs Route vs URL

```
These terms are often used interchangeably, but:

URL     → Full address: https://api.myapp.com/v1/questions/42
Path    → The part after domain: /v1/questions/42
Route   → Pattern matching a path: /questions/:id
Endpoint→ Route + HTTP method: GET /questions/:id
```

## What Makes A Good Endpoint

```
✅ Predictable: /users/{id}/posts follows the same pattern as /posts/{id}/comments
✅ Consistent naming: always plural, always lowercase, always hyphens
✅ Minimal: only expose what clients need
✅ Documented: every endpoint has a description, examples, and error codes
✅ Versioned: /v1/ prefix protects against breaking changes
```

question: What Is OAuth 2.0 And How Does The Flow Work?
answerGeneral: OAuth 2.0 is an authorisation framework that lets users grant third-party applications access to their account on another service without sharing their password. Example: 'Sign in with Google' on your app. The flow: your app redirects the user to Google with your client_id and requested scopes; user logs in to Google and grants permission; Google redirects back to your app with an authorisation code; your server exchanges the code for an access token (and optionally a refresh token) by calling Google's token endpoint with your client_secret; you use the access token to call Google APIs on the user's behalf. OAuth 2.0 has several grant types for different scenarios (Authorization Code, Client Credentials for server-to-server, PKCE for SPAs/mobile).
answerGeneralTr: OAuth 2.0, kullanıcıların şifrelerini paylaşmadan başka bir hizmetteki hesaplarına üçüncü taraf uygulamalar erişim vermesine izin veren bir yetkilendirme çerçevesidir. Örnek: uygulamanızda 'Google ile Giriş Yap'. Akış: uygulamanız kullanıcıyı client_id ve istenen kapsamlarla Google'a yönlendirir; kullanıcı Google'a giriş yapar ve izin verir; Google yetkilendirme koduyla uygulamanıza geri yönlendirir; sunucunuz kodu client_secret ile bir erişim token'ıyla değiştirir; erişim token'ını kullanıcı adına Google API'lerini çağırmak için kullanırsınız.
detailMd:
## OAuth 2.0 — Authorization Code Flow

## Step By Step

```
1. User clicks 'Sign in with Google'

2. App redirects to Google:
   https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/auth
     ?client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID
     &redirect_uri=https://yourapp.com/auth/callback
     &response_type=code
     &scope=email profile
     &state=random_csrf_token

3. User logs in to Google and grants permission

4. Google redirects to your callback:
   https://yourapp.com/auth/callback
     ?code=AUTH_CODE_HERE
     &state=random_csrf_token

5. Your server exchanges code for tokens:
   POST https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token
   { code, client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri, grant_type: 'authorization_code' }
   → { access_token, refresh_token, expires_in }

6. Use access_token to call Google APIs:
   GET https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v2/userinfo
   Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN
```

## Why The Code Exchange Matters

```
Why not return the token directly to the browser?

The auth code goes to the browser (URL) — it's short-lived and single-use.
The token exchange happens server-to-server with client_secret.
This means client_secret never touches the browser.

If token was returned to browser → JavaScript could steal it.
Code exchange via backend → token never exposed in URL.
```

## PKCE — For SPAs and Mobile (No Client Secret)

```
SPAs and mobile apps can't store client_secret securely.
PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) replaces client_secret:

1. App generates code_verifier (random string)
2. App sends code_challenge = SHA256(code_verifier) in auth request
3. Auth code returned as normal
4. Token exchange sends code_verifier (not secret)
5. Server verifies SHA256(code_verifier) === code_challenge

Even if auth code is intercepted, attacker doesn't have code_verifier.
```

question: How Do You Implement Server-Sent Events In Next.js?
answerGeneral: Server-Sent Events (SSE) provide a one-directional, real-time channel from server to browser over a standard HTTP connection. Unlike WebSockets (bidirectional, requires upgrade), SSE uses plain HTTP and is simpler to implement, automatically reconnects, and works through proxies. Use cases: live notifications, progress indicators, live feeds, AI token streaming. In Next.js App Router, you create a Route Handler that returns a ReadableStream with Content-Type: text/event-stream. The browser uses the EventSource API to subscribe. SSE messages follow a specific format: 'data: {...}\n\n'. Each message can optionally have an event type and ID for filtering and reconnection.
answerGeneralTr: Sunucu Tarafı Olayları (SSE), standart bir HTTP bağlantısı üzerinden sunucudan tarayıcıya tek yönlü, gerçek zamanlı bir kanal sağlar. WebSocket'lerin aksine (çift yönlü, yükseltme gerektirir), SSE düz HTTP kullanır, uygulaması daha basittir, otomatik olarak yeniden bağlanır ve proxy'ler üzerinden çalışır. Kullanım alanları: canlı bildirimler, ilerleme göstergeleri, canlı akışlar, AI token akışı. Next.js App Router'da, Content-Type: text/event-stream ile ReadableStream döndüren bir Route Handler oluşturursunuz.

question: How Do You Design A Search API?
answerGeneral: A well-designed search API considers: query input (full-text search string, filters, facets); response shape (hits with relevance scores, total count, facet counts for refinement UI); pagination (cursor or offset); sorting; highlighting matched text. For simple search, Postgres full-text search (tsvector + tsquery) is excellent and avoids an extra service. For complex search (faceting, relevance tuning, typo tolerance), Algolia, Elasticsearch, or Typesense are purpose-built. Key design decisions: does search happen server-side (more control, no client-side index) or client-side (instant, works offline with libraries like Fuse.js)?; how do you keep the search index in sync with your database (triggers, CDC, event-driven)?
answerGeneralTr: İyi tasarlanmış bir arama API'si şunları dikkate alır: sorgu girdisi (tam metin arama dizisi, filtreler, bölütler); yanıt şekli (alaka puanlarıyla isabetler, toplam sayı, bölüt sayıları); sayfalama; sıralama; eşleşen metnin vurgulanması. Basit arama için Postgres tam metin araması mükemmeldir ve ekstra bir hizmet gerektirmez. Karmaşık arama için Algolia, Elasticsearch veya Typesense amaçla inşa edilmiştir. Temel tasarım kararları: arama sunucu tarafında mı yoksa istemci tarafında mı gerçekleşiyor; arama dizinini veritabanınızla nasıl senkronize tutarsınız.
detailMd:
## Search API Design

## Request Design

```
GET /api/questions/search
  ?q=react hooks          → full-text query
  &topic=react&topic=nextjs → filter by topic (multi-value)
  &level=2&level=3        → filter by level
  &sort=relevance          → relevance | newest | level
  &limit=20
  &cursor=eyJpZCI6MTAwfQ  → cursor pagination

Response:
{
  "hits": [
    {
      "id": 801,
      "question": "What is <mark>useEffect</mark> in <mark>React hooks</mark>?",
      "topic": "react-hooks",
      "level": 2,
      "_score": 0.92
    }
  ],
  "total": 47,
  "facets": {
    "topic": { "react": 23, "react-hooks": 18, "nextjs": 6 },
    "level": { "1": 10, "2": 20, "3": 15, "4": 2 }
  },
  "pagination": { "nextCursor": "...", "hasMore": true }
}
```

## Postgres Full-Text Search

```typescript
// Great for most use cases — no extra service
export async function searchQuestions(query: string, filters: SearchFilters) {
  const { data } = await supabase.rpc('search_questions', {
    search_query: query,
    topic_filter: filters.topics,
    level_filter: filters.levels,
    result_limit: filters.limit,
  });
  return data;
}

// SQL function
-- CREATE FUNCTION search_questions(...)
-- SELECT id, question, topic, level,
--   ts_rank(search_vector, query) AS score,
--   ts_headline('english', question, query) AS highlighted
-- FROM questions,
--   plainto_tsquery('english', search_query) query
-- WHERE search_vector @@ query
--   AND (topic_filter IS NULL OR topic = ANY(topic_filter))
-- ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT result_limit;
```

## Keeping Index In Sync

```
Postgres tsvector:
  → Maintain with a trigger (auto-updates on INSERT/UPDATE)
  → Always in sync, no separate service

Algolia / Typesense:
  → Webhook on DB change → update index
  → CDC (Change Data Capture) with Debezium
  → Scheduled full re-index as fallback
```

question: What Is GraphQL Persisted Queries And Why Are They Used?
answerGeneral: Persisted queries (also called automatic persisted queries, APQ) address two GraphQL problems: large query payloads and security. Instead of sending the full query string on every request, the client sends only a hash of the query. The server looks up the pre-registered query by hash and executes it. Benefits: dramatically smaller payloads (a UUID instead of a 2KB query string); CDN cacheability (GET requests with a hash are cacheable by CDN); security (only pre-approved queries can run, blocking arbitrary query injection). Trade-offs: extra build step to register queries; less flexible for exploratory use. Used heavily in production GraphQL by Facebook, Shopify, and others.
answerGeneralTr: Kalıcı sorgular (APQ olarak da bilinir), iki GraphQL sorununu ele alır: büyük sorgu yükleri ve güvenlik. Her istekte tam sorgu dizesi göndermek yerine istemci yalnızca sorgunun hash'ini gönderir. Sunucu, önceden kaydedilmiş sorguyu hash'e göre arar ve çalıştırır. Faydaları: dramatik olarak daha küçük yükler; CDN önbelleklenebilirliği; güvenlik (yalnızca önceden onaylanmış sorgular çalışabilir). Dezavantajlar: sorguları kaydetmek için ek derleme adımı; araştırma kullanımı için daha az esnek.

question: How Do You Monitor And Observe An API In Production?
answerGeneral: Production API observability has three pillars: Metrics (quantitative measurements — request rate, error rate, latency percentiles p50/p95/p99, saturation); Logs (structured event records — each request with method, path, status, duration, user ID, correlation ID); Traces (end-to-end request flow across services — where time is spent, which service is slow). Key metrics to track: error rate (target < 0.1%), p99 latency (target < 500ms for most APIs), availability (target 99.9%). Set SLOs (Service Level Objectives) and alert on SLO burn rate, not just raw thresholds. Use OpenTelemetry for vendor-agnostic instrumentation. Pair with dashboards in Datadog, Grafana, or Honeycomb.
answerGeneralTr: Prodüksiyon API gözlemlenebilirliğinin üç sütunu vardır: Metrikler (nicel ölçümler — istek hızı, hata oranı, gecikme yüzdelik dilimleri p50/p95/p99); Günlükler (yapılandırılmış olay kayıtları — her istek için yöntem, yol, durum, süre, kullanıcı kimliği, korelasyon kimliği); İzler (servisler arasında uçtan uca istek akışı). Takip edilecek temel metrikler: hata oranı (hedef < %0,1), p99 gecikme, kullanılabilirlik. SLO'lar (Hizmet Düzeyi Hedefleri) belirleyin ve ham eşikler yerine SLO yanma oranı üzerinde uyarı verin. Satıcıdan bağımsız enstrümantasyon için OpenTelemetry kullanın.
